newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases on strong GDP figures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases on strong GDP figures.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were off 25 basis points in early trade on Monday on what dealers said was strong GDP data and demand from foreign investors.
"The GDP data confirm prior forecasts of an improving economy, especially as the figures were stronger than we expected, and that boosts the market," a fixed-income analyst said.
"We saw foreign buyers on Friday, and the GDP data will keep them coming," he added.
The Finance Ministry announced before trade opened that Mexican GDP had increased by 8.8 percent in the second quarter, compared with a year earlier.
A Reuters survey of 13 Mexico City financial houses had predicted a rise of 5.92 percent.
Another analyst said rates may have fallen due to anticipated demand for paper at Tuesday's primary central bank auction.
A sign of demand, he said, was Banco de Mexico's announcement on Friday that it had raised the amount of Cetes on offer to 4.2 billion pesos from 3.6 billion.

Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile down 50 basis points at 18.50 percent. Liquidity of 863 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation, in addition to an estimated 1.0 billion pesos in cash after the weekend.
He was referring to the Finance Ministry announcement that Mexican gross domestic rose by 8.8 percent year over year in the second quarter.

Rates also declined in anticipation of falling primary rates at Tuesday night's Mexican central bank auction, dealers said. Auction rates were expected to fall because of surplus liquidity, as scheduled maturities would far exceed the amount of paper on offer.
The central bank on Monday drained 338 million pesos from the market by assigning two repurchase agreements.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 60 basis points at 18.40 percent.
Liquidity of 138 million pesos was due to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
